extracted.intended_audience: students, architects, art historians, critics, and travelers interested in Venetian religious art and Byzantine architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for judging and designing religious art (mosaics, frescoes, church iconography) and for identifying Byzantine palatial architecture; emphasizes legibility, theological function, material use, and the balance between craft and devotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of religious feeling compensates for poor art
rubrics_metrics.description: "strength of religious feeling is capable of supplying for itself whatever is wanting in the rudest suggestions of art, and will either... purify what is coarse into inoffensiveness, or... raise what is feeble into impressiveness."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious emotion in the beholder can convert crude or technically weak representations into effective devotional images; association and belief in truth matter more than formal excellence for some audiences (example: child's strong impression from a rude colored print).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity to familiar types and incident selection wins admiration
rubrics_metrics.description: "The likeness to a beloved friend, the correspondence with a habitual conception, the freedom from any strange or offensive particularity, and, above all, an interesting choice of incident, will win admiration for a picture when the noblest efforts of religious imagination would otherwise fail of power."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conservative, recognizable depiction and carefully chosen, engaging incidents make religious images effective for popular devotion even if execution is imperfect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived truthfulness of representation reduces criticism of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: "the moment we believe the picture to be true, we complain little of its being ill-painted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If viewers accept an image as a truthful account (narrative), they are less likely to notice or object to technical flaws; convincing narrative content can outweigh poor technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative vs. invention: how the work is regarded
rubrics_metrics.description: "the painter of religious subject is no longer regarded as the narrator of a fact, but as the inventor of an idea."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern evaluation treats religious painting as creative invention; critics therefore focus on originality and faults of invention rather than on fidelity to a narrated event—this alters how religious art is judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and artless utterance are virtues in sacred art
rubrics_metrics.description: "a truly religious painter will very often be ruder, quainter, simpler, and more faulty in his manner of working... it is in [artless utterance] that all noble schools of art have been cradled."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpolished, direct expression can be more spiritually effective than highly refined technique; churches historically valued simple, sincere expression for devotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural imaginative power > academic polish
rubrics_metrics.description: "people mistake the polish for the power... the real gift in him is utterly independent of all such accomplishments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prioritize learned academic skill (foreshortening, perspective, anatomy) over innate imaginative gifts; overvaluing polish can suppress powerful but untrained artists whose work serves devotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid evidences of skill that distract from the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: "they were not adorned with any evidences of skill or science, such as might withdraw the attention from their subjects."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical displays, superfluous ornament, or conspicuous craftsmanship that draw attention to the art itself undermine the devotional purpose; design should keep focus on the theological subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for legibility and intelligibility in situ
rubrics_metrics.description: "bright coloring and disregard of chiaroscuro cannot be regarded as imperfections, since they are the only means by which the figures could be rendered clearly intelligible in the distance and darkness of the vaulting."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating church mosaics or vault imagery, prioritize color, contrast, and simplicity of form to ensure figures are readable at distance and in dim architectural settings; conventional painterly 'rules' may need to be set aside for visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective religious art lies between idolatry and pure craftsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: "Effective religious art, therefore, has always lain, and I believe must always lie, between the two extremes— of barbarous idol-fashioning on one side, and magnificent craftsmanship on the other."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal devotional art avoids both crude fetishistic idol-making and art so exquisite that it diverts worshippers' devotion into admiration of skill; media like missal painting, glass-painting, rude sculpture, mosaics, frescoes and tempera historically occupy this balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monumentality and persistence to command attention
rubrics_metrics.description: mosaics "covered the walls and roofs of the churches with inevitable lustre; they could not be ignored or escaped from; their size rendered them majestic, their distance mysterious, their color attractive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-scale, permanent media (mosaic covering walls/roofs) are effective because they are unavoidable and continually present to worshippers; scale and permanence support religious instruction and awe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inscriptions must be legible and abundant as didactic tools
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our eyes are now familiar and wearied with writing; ... the old architect was sure of readers. He knew that every one would be glad to decipher all that he wrote; ... the more he gave them, the more grateful would the people be."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architectural writing and inscriptions should be large, clear, and plentiful to teach and remind worshippers; text integrated into building functions as a 'stone manuscript' for congregations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconographic program should instruct catechumens
rubrics_metrics.description: The atrium was reserved for unbaptized persons to contemplate the great facts of the Old Testament... the order of the subjects ... closing with the Fall of the Manna, in order to mark to the catechumen the insufficiency of the Mosaic covenant for salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence and selection of subjects (e.g., Old Testament scenes culminating in typological conclusions) should be pedagogically arranged to teach specific theological points to new converts and the illiterate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central placement and hierarchy of doctrinal images
rubrics_metrics.description: The mosaic of the first dome... represents the effusion of the Holy Spirit... the second cupola... is entirely occupied by the subject of the Ascension... the third cupola... represents the witness of the Old Testament to Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position the most theologically central images (Pentecost, Ascension, Resurrection) in the most prominent, visible architectural loci (central domes, main cupola) so the building's spatial program reinforces doctrinal priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic coherence: align figures, symbols and inscriptions to doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneath the circle of the apostles... are represented the Christian virtues... beneath them... the four Evangelists... and, finally, beneath their feet, ... the four rivers of Paradise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iconography should pair figures, virtues, and symbols in a coherent theological hierarchy (e.g., apostles → virtues → evangelists → rivers) so that visual associations reinforce doctrinal meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of art with civic life and continual moral testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: It was at once a type of the Redeemed Church of God, and a scroll for the written word of God... Men met there from all countries of the earth... above the crowd... the glory of the temple, attesting... that there was one treasure which the merchantmen might buy without a price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious art and architecture should be publicly legible and morally instructive, serving as a continual reminder and testimony in civic spaces; visibility to the populace helps bind civic identity to religious testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of materials to convey sacred meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: And whether honored as the Church or as the Bible, was it not fitting that neither the gold nor the crystal should be spared in the adornment of it; that, as the symbol of the Bride, the building... should be of jasper, and the foundations... garnished with all manner of precious stones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use costly or luminous materials (gold, crystal, precious stones) deliberately to symbolize sacred truths (e.g., Bride, Scripture) rather than for mere ostentation; materials should support the building's didactic and devotional aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byzantine palaces: identifying formal features
rubrics_metrics.description: They all agree in being round-arched and incrusted with marble... six... have continuous arcades along their entire fronts... arcades divided... into a centre and wings; both by greater size in the midmost arches, and by the alternation of shafts in the centre, with pilasters, or with small shafts, at the flanks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for recognizing Byzantine palatial form include round arches, marble incrustation, continuous arcades, central emphasis by larger mid arches, and alternation of shafts/pilasters; use these morphological signs to deduce original disposition despite ruin or restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize intelligibility for common people over refined detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The walls of the church necessarily became the poor man's Bible, and a picture was more easily read upon the walls than a chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design imagery for immediate comprehension by general worshippers (including the illiterate); simple, bold images that can be 'read' at a glance serve communal instruction better than intricate details only legible to specialists.
